decisionsTitle: The volunteer badge: a free-text line and a space for the marker
decisionsSection:
**The owner, 2026-10-15, about the badge of §764:** «Pe ecusonul voluntarilor vreau să pot da și free-text sau să pot scrie undeva cu markerul, e cel mai simplu.» He said «YOLO»: the open points are decided here, by the build.

**Decision.** Two optional sections in «Cum arată ecusonul», each behind a tick box of its own (a `CheckboxField`, never a toggle), each in the designer's own section pattern (`Panel`, level 5, a glyph, a closed line), drawn through the one geometry (`badge-geometry.ts`) by the pdfkit sheet, the Satori picture and so every preview, on both presets and every custom size.

- **«Text liber».** One typed line of the club's own words, in Romanian and English or neither (the pair rule of §352; the badge prints the language it is printed in), at most 60 characters (`BADGE_FREE_TEXT_MAX`). **Where:** its own row of white under the role's band, between the band and the writing area — small, centred, in the body ink. Not inside the role's band: that carries «VOLUNTAR» and the role's name and changes colour per role, and a third line there would crush the two that matter. The row is a tenth of the content's height, like the telephone's (`BADGE_LAYOUT.freeShare`); the line is fitted by `badgeFit` from 0.62 of its row down to 4.5 points and only then cut with «…» — a 60-character line fits a 60 mm badge without shrinking, only wide capitals shrink it. It is the club's words, the same on every badge: no personal data.
- **«Spațiu pentru marker».** A second white writing area, **beside «Nume:», not under it**: a strip is short and wide, and the height is what is scarce (the writing area keeps its 10 mm). The writing area is shared — the name's area at the left, the marker's at its right (38% of the width, never under 16 mm; the name's never under 24 mm; 2 mm between them and a faint divider) — with an optional label typed by the club («Tură», «Zona»; at most 20 characters, Romanian and English or neither, printed with a colon after it as «Nume:» has) at its top left and one faint line at the name's own line height. The marker's line is always drawn — it is the section's whole purpose — while the name's line stays the writing section's own tick. The PDF is blank there: it is written at the desk.
- **Rows and the size.** `badgeRows` has a free-text row (after the role's band) when the club writes one; when the rows under the bands leave the writing area under 10 mm the header and the role's band give up their share in proportion, as before, and `squeeze` says how much of it they kept. **A size too small for everything ticked is refused at the save** — `BADGE_SIZE_TOO_SMALL`, `badgeSizeRefusal` — when the bands would keep under four fifths of their height (`BADGE_BANDS_MIN_SHARE`): the sentence names what does not fit («linia de text liber, telefonul coordonatorului»), the size, and the least height at the same width. In numbers: 90 × 35 and 100 × 40 take everything; on a custom size the free-text line and the telephone together need 34 mm of height, whatever the width; each alone fits at every size the bounds allow, so nothing a design drew before is refused. The marker area takes width, not height, and the bounds keep both areas their least width at every height (a test sweeps them); the designer says the limit in words beside the size, before the save. The refusal is a form refusal naming the height's box, with every box kept; it is not drawn crushed and not quietly changed.
- **The design.** Six optional keys in the one `events.badge_design` jsonb — `showFreeText`, `freeTextRo`, `freeTextEn`, `showMarker`, `markerLabelRo`, `markerLabelEn` — **no migration**. The reader (`readBadgeDesign`) takes them as it takes the rest: a design without them reads both off and draws as before (`BADGE_DRAWING_VERSION` stays 1, since the same design draws the same), and a value of the wrong type is dropped as the platform's own, never a throw — and `badgeDesignDropped` names it, so the designer says beside the section that a saved value could not be read and was left out. The event's file carries the keys under `badges.design` (the diff names each), read forgivingly at the file's reading; a copy keeps them. «Text liber» ticked with nothing written is refused (a tick that prints nothing); a text typed while its tick is off is kept, as the telephone's label is.

**Refused, and why.** The line inside the role's band (above). The marker area under «Nume:» (height). A line per role (the badge is already per role by name and colour; words per role would be another settings surface for one line a club writes once). Rich text or a second line (a badge is read at a glance, and a second line is the marker area). Shrinking the writing area under 10 mm to make everything fit (the name written in marker is the badge's purpose).
changelogLine: - **A free-text line and a space for the marker on the volunteer badge** — two optional sections in «Cum arată ecusonul»: one small line of the club's own words under the role's band, and a second white area beside «Nume:» with an optional label (such as «Tură») and a line for the marker. The sheet and the preview draw both, and a size with no room for everything ticked is refused in words, naming what does not fit and how tall a badge it needs. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Given «Cum arată ecusonul», when «Text liber» is ticked with a line written in Romanian and in English (at most 60 characters) or «Spațiu pentru marker» is ticked with an optional label in both languages (at most 20), then «Salvează ecusonul» keeps them in `events.badge_design` with the other settings and audits the keys changed; a text in one language only, and «Text liber» ticked with nothing written, are refused naming the box with every box kept; the preview, the sheet and each role's picture draw the line small and centred under the role's band and a second white area beside «Nume:» — a faint divider, the label with its colon at its top left, one faint line at the name's own height, blank in the PDF — through the one layout, on both presets and every custom size, the writing area never under 10 mm and the name's and the marker's areas never under 24 and 16 mm (2026-10-15, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN). Verification: unit `volunteers/badge-free-text.test.ts`, `volunteers/badges-pdf.test.ts`; integration `volunteers/badges.test.ts`; e2e `volunteer-badges.spec.ts`.

Given a size on which the free-text line and the coordinator's telephone, both ticked, would leave the header and the role's band under four fifths of their height (a custom size under 34 mm tall), when the design is saved, then it is refused with `BADGE_SIZE_TOO_SMALL`, a sentence in the language of the page naming what does not fit, the size and the least height at the same width, naming the height's box, with nothing kept; each of the two alone, the marker's area and both presets are never refused for size, so a design saved before is never refused by it, and the designer says the height needed beside the size before the save (2026-10-15, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN). Verification: unit `volunteers/badge-free-text.test.ts`; integration `volunteers/badges.test.ts`; e2e `volunteer-badges.spec.ts`.

Given a badge design stored, or an event file made, before the free-text line and the marker area, when it is read, then both are off and it draws exactly as it did, saving the same boxes again changes nothing, and a stored value of the wrong type is read as the platform's own — never a throw — and named in the designer beside its section; the six keys travel in the event's file under `badges.design`, the diff naming each, and in a copy of the event (2026-10-15, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN). Verification: unit `volunteers/badge-free-text.test.ts`; integration `volunteers/badges.test.ts`, `events/event-json.test.ts`.

batchLine: the volunteer badge: a free-text line and a marker area
